page.layout: Top: two circular medallion engravings with portrait heads and legends around their rims, side by side. Below them: one column of running text, with the entries PROMETHEUS, ATLAS and ALTADAS as paragraphs. Running head centred at top, page number at top left. Ornamental fleuron at the foot. No margin notes.

main_text.p: PROMETHEUS, Iapeti atque Asiæ filius, propterea fertur de luto formasse homines, quia optimus sapientiæ doctor fuisse perhibetur, ut sentit Augustinus. Huic inventionē ferrei anuli tribuebat antiquitas, vinculúmque id, non gestamen intelligi volebat. Lactātius re vera primum omniū simulachrum hominis formasse de pingui & molli luto Prometheum scribit, ab eoque natam primò artem, statuas, & simulachra fingendi. Hic ignem Ioui dicitur furatus, quòd ex ferro, & silice ignem extundere docuerit, servareq; in ferula. Videto Augustinū de civita. Dei lib.18.cap.8. Lactan.lib.2.cap.11. Pli.lib.13.cap.1.
ATLAS, Promethei frater, primus Sphæram Astrologiamq; invenisse dicitur. inde locus fabulæ datus, quòd cœlum humeris fulciret. Vergil.6. Aeneidos,

p.i: —Vbi cœlifer Atlas Axem humero torquet, stellis ardentibus aptum.

main_text.p: ALTADAS XII. Assyriorum rex, horum temporibus extitit, ut ait Cassiodorus. Hic regnare cœpit anno mundi 2263. ante Christum natum 1699. Huius institutum fuit ut divitiis & gloria, aliena stultitia & miseria à maioribus suis partis, quoad viveret, frueretur. Vide Bero. lib. 5. Huius ætate Galates apud Celtas, & Vandalus apud Thuyscones regnauit.

page.notes: The two medallions are engravings. Their legends are printed on the rims: left "PROMETHEVS" (split as PROME / THEVS), right "ATLAS MAVRVS". The small mark at the left margin beside the ATLAS line is a stray printer's mark, not text. The ornament at the foot is a fleuron, not text. Spelling "PROMPTV" and "ICONVM" in the running head and "PROMETHEVS"/"MAVRVS" in the legends are shown with u/v adjusted per the rules. "Pli." in the Plinius reference is read as printed and may be "Plin." in the scan.
